**Given Data:**
- Alternator connection: Star
- Line Voltage ($V_L$) = $400\text{ V}$
- Load connection: Delta
- Load resistance per phase ($R_{ph}$) = $10\ \Omega$
- Load inductive reactance per phase ($X_{Lph}$) = $20\ \Omega$

**1. Load Impedance ($Z_{ph}$):**
$$Z_{ph} = \sqrt{R_{ph}^2 + X_{Lph}^2} = \sqrt{10^2 + 20^2} = \sqrt{100 + 400} = \sqrt{500} = 22.36\ \Omega$$

**2. Load Phase Voltage ($V_{L,load}$):**
The load is connected across the same $400\text{ V}$ lines, so load phase voltage equals line voltage:
$$V_{ph(load)} = V_L = 400\text{ V}$$

**3. Load Phase Current ($I_{ph(load)}$):**
$$I_{ph(load)} = \frac{V_{ph(load)}}{Z_{ph}} = \frac{400}{22.36} = 17.89\text{ A}$|

**(i) Line Current of the Alternator ($I_L$):**
For a delta load, line current is $\sqrt{3}$ times the phase current:
$$I_L = \sqrt{3} \times I_{ph(load)} = \sqrt{3} \times 17.89 = 30.98\text{ A}$|

**(ii) Power Factor ($\cos \phi$):**
$$\cos \phi = \frac{R_{ph}}{Z_{ph}} = \frac{10}{22.36} = 0.447 \text{ (lagging)}$$

**(iii) Output Power ($P$):**
$$P = \sqrt{3} \times V_L \times I_L \times \cos \phi = \sqrt{3} \times 400 \times 30.98 \times 0.447 = 9600\text{ W} = 9.6\text{ kW}$|

**(iv) kVA Rating of the Alternator:**
$$\text{kVA} = \frac{\sqrt{3} \times V_L \times I_L}{1000} = \frac{\sqrt{3} \times 400 \times 30.98}{1000} = 21.47\text{ kVA}$|
proTip: Always check whether the load is star or delta connected to correctly relate phase and line quantities.
